description: Emergence of sedentary village life, early ceramic production, and initial social differentiation.
Mesoamerican equivalent of the Formative; first monumental centres and regional ceramic traditions.
Teotihuacan ascendancy and wide circulation of Thin Orange ware across Mesoamerica.
Peak of lowland Maya and highland Mexican state formation; highly standardised serving wares.
Regional polychrome traditions proliferate; intensified inter-site exchange.
Post-Teotihuacan reorganisation; northern frontier centres such as La Quemada flourish.
Political restructuring in the Maya lowlands; slate wares dominate northern Yucatán.
Widespread trade networks, Plumbate and Fine Orange circulation, new political capitals.
Central Panamanian polychrome horizon associated with the Sitio Conte cemetery.
Early polychrome development on the Pacific slope of Panama.
Monumental coastal architecture in Peru; plain and incised utilitarian assemblages.
Hohokam Sedentary period; red-on-buff decorated wares at their widest distribution.
Hohokam Classic period; platform mounds, adobe compounds, and the spread of Salado polychromes.
